advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm intended treatment of non-{success,failure,cancelled,skipped} result strings (neutral/timed_out/action_required) in render().
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:122: only `{"cancelled", "skipped"}` are treated as unavailable
scripts/main_health_report.py:117-118 docstring enumerates results as `success`, `failure`, `cancelled`, `skipped` — but GitHub also emits `neutral`/`timed_out`/`action_required`
A `timed_out` job would be treated as RED, and a `neutral` (non-failing) job would also be treated as RED though it is not a genuine failure
advisory.finding: The UNAVAILABLE renderer classifies any non-success/non-failure result as incomplete only for `cancelled`/`skipped`; other GitHub result strings (e.g. `neutral`, `timed_out`, `action_required`, `stale`) fall through to the RED path, which may or may not be intended.
scenarios: A gating job times out or returns neutral: rendered as RED (failure) rather than acknowledged as incomplete

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `UNAVAILABLE` in out (and `RED`/`GREEN` not in out) for the empty jobs={} case.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:122 adds `if not jobs or any(result in {"cancelled", "skipped"} ...): return _render_unavailable(...)`
tests/unit/test_main_health_report.py:66-67 `out = report.render(ref_name="main", head_sha="abc123def456", jobs={})` then only `assert "GREEN" not in out`
Named violating input: jobs={} — the added line routes empty to UNAVAILABLE, but the test does not assert 'UNAVAILABLE' in out, so a regression rendering empty as RED goes undetected.
advisory.finding: The empty-job-set test does not assert the newly introduced empty->UNAVAILABLE behavior; it only checks 'GREEN' not in out, so it would still pass if an empty job set incorrectly rendered as RED.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_an_empty_job_set_is_not_treated_as_green, add `assert "UNAVAILABLE" in out` and `assert "RED" not in out` alongside the existing GREEN check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the unavailable output includes the per-job result row (e.g. `| golden-path | cancelled |`) for the cancelled/skipped case.
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:140-142 adds `if jobs: lines += ["", "| job | result |", "| --- | --- |"]` and `lines += [f"| {name} | {result} |" ...]`
tests/unit/test_main_health_report.py:61-62 asserts only `"UNAVAILABLE" in out` and `"GREEN" not in out and "RED" not in out`
Named violating input: jobs={**_ALL_GREEN, 'golden-path': 'cancelled'} produces a row `| golden-path | cancelled |` that no assertion checks.
advisory.finding: The new _render_unavailable job-result table (added lines) is not asserted by any test; the cancelled/skipped test checks only the UNAVAILABLE heading and GREEN/RED absence.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_a_cancelled_or_skipped_gate_reports_unavailable, add `assert f"| golden-path | {unproven} |" in out`.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a genuine `failure` gate still renders RED even when other gates are cancelled/skipped (only treat as UNAVAILABLE when NO job failed).
evidence: scripts/main_health_report.py:122: `if not jobs or any(result in {"cancelled", "skipped"} for result in jobs.values()):`
scripts/main_health_report.py:124-130: the red branch (with bisect recipe) is only reached when no job is cancelled/skipped

When a gating job fails, GitHub Actions commonly marks dependent/sibling jobs `skipped` or `cancelled`; such a run has both a `failure` and a `skipped`/`cancelled` value, so it takes the UNAVAILABLE branch and never emits RED

Module docstring (test_main_health_report.py:4-7) states the summary must hand the responder a lower bound and runnable bisect on an ALREADY-failing run — precisely the case this ordering can now suppress
blocking.finding: A run containing a genuine `failure` gate alongside any `cancelled`/`skipped` gate now renders UNAVAILABLE instead of RED, because the UNAVAILABLE branch is checked before the red path and matches on ANY cancelled/skipped job. This masks a real failure and suppresses the bisect recipe.
scenarios: A build-and-test job fails and its downstream golden-path/artifact-probe jobs are auto-skipped: main is genuinely broken but the summary says UNAVAILABLE with no bisect recipe
blocking.suggested_fix: Guard the UNAVAILABLE branch on the absence of any `failure`: `if not jobs or (not any(r == "failure" for r in jobs.values()) and any(r in {"cancelled","skipped"} for r in jobs.values())):` so a real failure wins over an incomplete-observation verdict.
